summary:
I designed the recorded finger-shape subsystem (D4) and the sideways whole-page setting (D5). It is grounded in the code at 89893aa, the five code maps, the final plan, 16 device logs, and a C prototype I built and ran, which covers the matcher, the gates and a synthetic corpus.

Capture: a one-finger shape is a finger that lands on the idle page (OWN_LINK) and stays the only contact, fingertip-sized, with the pen away for the whole touch. It counts as a shape once it has moved 6 mm, but only after 150 ms (the window in which a second finger turns it into a two-finger gesture) and only if it started moving within 400 ms of landing. That keeps it apart from a tap (2.5 mm slop) and from the 600 ms link hold. The shape ends at lift. It must be at least 20 mm across with a path of at least 30 mm, must take under 2.5 s, and must not pause for 0.5 s (a pause cancels it).

Recognizer: integer $P point-cloud matching over 32 resampled points. It ignores where a shape starts and which way it is drawn, so a circle drawn either way is one gesture. It does not normalize rotation and only tolerates 10 degrees, so V and ^ stay 156 per mille apart. The score is the mean point distance as a fraction of the shape's size. Each gesture gets its own accept threshold of 70 to 95 per mille, derived from its 2-3 samples, and a match needs a clear margin over the second best. An unknown shape does nothing. The arithmetic is integer only, so the Kindle, the Mac simulator and the runner give the same result.

The main finding: a single slip of the finger draws one-turn shapes. In the prototype, recorded V, <, check mark, L, U and C shapes fired on 3-6% of synthetic thumb arcs and single-turn slips. The recorder therefore checks each new shape against a fixed bank of about 1500-2000 slips (one-turn slides and arcs at every orientation) and refuses any shape a slip can reach, saying why. With that rule: 0 of 12,000 swipes and 0 of 12,000 thumb arcs fired, 2 of 12,000 single-turn slips fired, 0 wrong-action fires in 6,200 tries, and 92.6% of shapes were accepted under deliberately harsh variation. Shapes with two turns or a loop stay available (N, Z, S, circle, zigzag, alpha, square, 2, spiral). Synthetic palm-like drifts still fired 29 times in 12,000, which is why the touch-size, palm and pen gates are required and why the device writing traces are the real test.

Recording, in Settings > Gestures: draw the shape 2-3 times into three slots. Each refusal names its reason (too small, too slow, too straight, too easy to make by accident, not like the first, too close to another action's shape, pen near). A matching shape gets "That is the shape for Undo. Use moves it here." Each row shows the shape as a thumbnail; holding a row clears it, and Reset asks first when shapes would be lost.

On the page: a dotted trail drawn with DU, never ink. On a match it is cleaned by one GL16 and a small toast names the action. On a reject it thins to half its dots (DU), then fades out with a GL16 250 ms later; there is no flash in either case.

Storage: gestures.ini lines of the form shape.<action>=1,N,<128 hex>... sit beside the touch.* and pen.* overlay keys. Each action can hold one shape, at most 32 in all; lines from newer versions are kept and written back.

D5: settings.ini landscape_fit=1, on by default (the owner should be told). Sideways, the resting view becomes the whole page, so nothing scrolls and two-finger swipes work everywhere. Pinch zoom still works, and page turns, rotation and Fit page all return to the whole page. The toggle is a new row in the Display sheet and the action landscape-fit in the Pages group. It ships in P2; finger shapes ship in P4, after the touch traces fix T_palm and the thresholds.
design:
RECORDED FINGER SHAPES (D4) AND THE SIDEWAYS WHOLE PAGE (D5)
Design for Grimoire beta.5 features at 89893aa, with the keyboard lane's helpers (1db4f96) assumed. It extends the final plan (index-hook-final-plan-2026-10-27.json) and replaces its answer to question 6 ("a fixed set, nothing free-form"), as ruling D4 requires. The plan's fixed vocabulary stays for multi-finger swipes, taps and pen buttons. Recorded shapes are a new, separate source.

Evidence used:
- the touch code map (input_evdev.c, the editor's finger handling, the runner);
- the 16 device logs in ~/KindleLab/evidence (767 one-finger downs, 74 one-finger drags);
- a prototype of the matcher, the gates and a synthetic corpus, written and run for this design: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ganten/581d011a-0434-4f33-bbe0-96eefdeceb65/scratchpad/fshape/proto.c, final.c and bank.c, with drags.py for the log statistics.
The numbers below come from those runs. They are synthetic or from logs with read-time stamps, so they are targets to confirm on the device, not frozen constants.

======================================================================
0. NAMES AND PLACE IN THE PLAN
======================================================================
- UI name: "finger shape" / "figura con el dedo". It never says just "shape", because Smart shapes (P5, pen) own "Shapes" / "Formas inteligentes".
- Code:
  - src/fingershape.c/.h: pure, in CORE_SRC, built and host-tested like pensync.c. Integer math only, no libm, no allocation, no clock.
  - src/fingershape_synth.c: the synthetic shape and slip generator. It is linked only into the simulator, the runner and the tests.
- Binding source: SHAPE joins KEY | PAD | TOUCH | PEN in the registry's sources mask (plan step 16). Dispatch is editor_shortcut_at(a, action, x, y, SRC_SHAPE).
- Phases:
  - The sideways whole-page setting ships in P2, with the two-finger gestures it exists for.
  - Finger shapes ship in P4, with Settings > Gestures. That is after the P1 touch traces have been read: T_palm and the gate constants are frozen from them.
  - P1 gains two small additions: a touch-trace file and per-touch facts from touchgest.

======================================================================
1. WHO DECIDES WHAT (the layers)
======================================================================
- touchgest.c (P1, pure). It owns contact-level facts the editor cannot see, and stamps IN_TOUCH_DOWN/MOVE/UP with:
  - k_ms: the SYN_REPORT kernel time, in now_ms()'s clock through pensync_ms. Today emit_touch stamps read time (input_evdev.c:444-451), and a backlog after a render bunches it.
  - value bit 0, TOUCH_F_BROAD: this contact's TOUCH_MAJOR has exceeded T_palm at some frame this session. T_palm comes from the P1 log.
  - value bit 1, TOUCH_F_CANCEL: the off-screen cancel. x and y stay at -10000, as cancel_touch does today (input_evdev.c:670-678), so old code keeps working.
  Everything else it already does: the second-contact rules, MT_TOOL_PALM suppression, the global pen window, and suppression until all contacts lift. A shape session can be cancelled at any moment by the off-screen UP.
- fingershape.c (pure). It holds:
  - the capture state machine and its buffer;
  - the gates;
  - normalization, the $P matcher and the per-gesture thresholds;
  - the record-time checks (consistency, separation, the slip bank);
  - the one-finger straight-swipe classifier (touch.1.<dir>, plan step 19, moved here because it shares the capture);
  - the gestures.ini shape-line codec;
  - the trail and thumbnail drawing helpers, which use canvas.h only.
- editor.c owns the UI facts. The finger must have landed on the page as OWN_LINK (editor.c:2433-2438), not on the panel or a sheet. It also checks which menus are open, keeps the trail's rect, and dispatches. library.c (MOD_GESTURES) hosts the same capture for recording.
- gesturemap.c (plan step 7) owns the bindings: the touch.* and pen.* overlay plus the new shape.* lines.

======================================================================
2. CAPTURE: TELLING A SHAPE FROM EVERYTHING ELSE A FINGER DOES
======================================================================
A one-finger session runs the state machine below. Today's tap and link behaviour is untouched: link_press, press_move's 30 px slop (ui.c:469-474), link_follow on an unmoved lift (editor.c:2455-2459), and link_hold after LINK_HOLD_MS 600 (editor.c:2592).

ARMED. Capture happens only when all of these hold:
- settings gestures is on (the plan's master switch);
- at least one one-finger binding exists: a shape, or a touch.1.* swipe;
- no keyboard is open;
- the editor is open, with no sheet in front except the Links bar (see 7.5).
When not armed, nothing changes from today, and no trail is ever drawn.

IDLE -> PENDING: the finger lands on the page. editor_event makes it OWN_LINK, and fs_begin records the landing point and k_ms. Points are buffered from the landing, so a shape includes its own start.
- Buffer: 256 raw points. Past that it decimates by 2 in place. 2.5 s at 80 Hz is 200 points.
- Cost: O(1) per IN_TOUCH_MOVE.

PENDING -> DRAWING, when all of these hold:
- the finger has moved 6 mm (71 px, Euclidean) from the landing point. The tap slop of 2.5 mm stays as it is, so the band from 2.5 to 6 mm still does nothing, as today;
- at least 150 ms have passed since landing. That is the plan's two-finger landing window, and 79% of the logged cancelled two-finger landings fell inside it. A two-finger swipe whose second finger lands late therefore never flashes a shape trail first;
- the 6 mm exit came within 400 ms of landing (the "lead").
In the logs, deliberate one-finger drags left the slop at a median of about 74 ms, and nearly all within 140 ms. One drag started after a 741 ms rest, and the lead rule refuses it.

Why 400 ms: it is below the 600 ms link hold, with a margin. A finger still at 400 ms can only become a tap or a hold, never a shape. A finger resting and then sliding (a grip thumb, a hand settling) is not a shape.

PENDING -> DEAD, silently with nothing drawn, when:
- the 6 mm exit comes after 400 ms ("late start");
- the link hold fires;
- TOUCH_F_BROAD arrives (palm-sized contact).

DRAWING -> FINISH: the real lift (IN_TOUCH_UP without TOUCH_F_CANCEL). The gates run first, then the matcher (sections 3 and 4).

DRAWING -> ABORT on the off-screen cancel. touchgest sends it when:
- a second contact lands, at any delay: under 150 ms it becomes a gesture, 150-400 ms a zoom or pan, over 400 ms a palm (input_evdev.c:719-737);
- MT_TOOL_PALM is flagged (708-711);
- the pen arrives (input_evdev.c:476-480, made a real cancel in plan step 2).
The trail goes away at once (see 7.4). Nothing fires.

DRAWING -> DEAD, while the finger is still down:
- landing + 2500 ms has passed;
- the finger stays within 1.5 mm (18 px) for 500 ms. This is the deliberate escape hatch: "hold still to cancel".
editor_tick checks both on wall time, only when App.input_drained is true, as the plan does for holds, so a queued lift is never read as a pause. The trail thins at that moment, and the rest of the touch is ignored until the lift.

How each competitor is excluded, and by what:
- Tap: under 6 mm, so it never leaves PENDING. Link follow is exactly today's.
- Link hold (600 ms): needs an unmoved finger. A shape needs movement before 400 ms. The two are exclusive by construction.
- A finger starting on the panel, a sheet, the card, the Pages view or the tool picker: it gets another owner (editor.c:2381-2431), so it is never OWN_LINK and never captured. A paper-sheet tap outside dismisses the sheet and swallows the gesture, as today.
- Palm:
  - MT_TOOL_PALM suppresses everything until all contacts lift;
  - TOUCH_F_BROAD kills the session;
  - a palm that landed while the pen was near stays suppressed until it lifts, even if it slides after the pen leaves. T.suppressed clears only when every contact has lifted (input_evdev.c:754, 762-766). A resting writing hand is therefore never a shape.
- Hand resting while writing:
  - the global pen window: single fingers are ignored while P.prox, and for 1 s after the pen leaves (input_evdev.c:667);
  - the persistence above;
  - the second-contact rule: a hand usually makes several contacts;
  - the slip bank (section 5), so a hand's one-turn skid cannot match a recorded shape.
- The start of a two-finger gesture or pinch: the 150 ms trail delay, plus the cancel on any second contact. pinch() already drops an OWN_LINK finger at PINCH_BEGIN (editor.c:2281-2285); it also aborts the shape.
- Pen near: there are no IN_TOUCH events at all inside the pen window, and pen arrival cancels. In record mode, touchgest reports a single-finger landing it suppressed as a rejection, so the card can say "The pen is near: move it away."
- v2, after the trace: a resting grip contact excluded as in the plan's rule 6 (still within 3 mm for 300 ms before the shape finger landed, at least 40 mm away, rejected if it moves). v1 is stricter: exactly one contact for the whole session.

======================================================================
3. THE GATES (identical at runtime and in recording; one header, a unit test asserts they are shared)
======================================================================
On the lift, in screen mm through ui_px (11.8 px/mm). A shape's size is independent of the page zoom, so shapes work at any zoom.
- Frames: at least 8 raw points.
- Size: bounding box major side of at least 20 mm (236 px), and a path of at least 30 mm (354 px).
- Time: landing to lift at most 2500 ms. Mean speed over the drawn part (path length / time from the 6 mm exit to the lift) at least 50 mm/s. A 30 mm path in 0.6 s passes.
- Not a line: the largest distance of any point from the start-end chord must be at least 15% of max(chord, box major side). When the chord is under a quarter of the path, the distance to the start point is used instead (closed shapes).
  - A line goes to the one-finger swipe classifier: touch.1.<up|down|left|right> needs at least 30 mm within 600 ms, within 30 degrees of an axis (the plan's rule).
  - Otherwise it does nothing.
  - In the logs, 14 of the 17 drags that reach the size gate are straight. They can never reach the shape matcher.
- Not tangled: path length at most 5x the box diagonal. Scribbles and scrubbing are refused.
- Context: TOUCH_F_BROAD never seen; no cancel; armed.

======================================================================
4. THE RECOGNIZER
======================================================================
CHOICE: $P (Vatavu, Anthony and Wobbrock's point-cloud matcher), single stroke, in integer arithmetic, with early abandoning.

Why not $1 or Protractor: they compare points in drawing order.
- A closed shape started at a different point fails ($1 is known for this with circles and squares).
- A shape drawn the other way fails.
- $1's non-uniform scaling distorts flat shapes.
- On e-ink the trail lags about 0.2-0.35 s behind the finger, so users cannot steer start point and direction by sight. Order sensitivity becomes a steady source of "it did not work".

Why not DTW: also order-sensitive, also O(n^2), and harder to threshold.

Why not $Q: $Q's lookup-table lower bounds exist for hundreds of templates. We have at most 96 (32 shapes x 3 samples) and match once per lift. Plain $P with early abandoning measures fast enough (below). $Q-style bounds are the documented fallback if the device bench exceeds 25 ms.

Normalization (fs_normalize):
- Resample to N = 32 points equidistant along the path (16x fixed-point px). At 75-80 Hz a 0.4 s shape has about 30 raw points; 32 is $P's usual count and keeps O(n^2) cheap.
- Translate the centroid to 0.
- Scale uniformly, never per axis: the larger box side becomes 512 units. The shape's aspect is kept; position and size are discarded.
- Coordinates are int16, distances int32, sums int64, and square roots by an integer isqrt. The same input therefore gives the same score on the Kindle (armhf), the Mac and the runner. Float contraction differs between those compilers; integers do not. Tests can then assert exact scores.

Distance:
- $P greedy cloud matching. Starts every 5 points (floor(sqrt(32))) in both directions, keeping the minimum.
- Weights fall from 1 to 1/32 along the matching order.
- Score D = weighted mean point distance / 512 x 1000, in per mille of the shape's size. D = 80 means "on average each point is 8% of the shape's size from where it should be": 2.4 mm on a 30 mm shape.

Direction, rotation, scale, position:
- Direction and start point: ignored by construction (a point cloud). A circle drawn clockwise and one drawn anticlockwise are ONE gesture. Recording the other direction for another action is refused as "That is the shape for Undo. Use moves it here." Grimoire matches what a shape looks like, not how it was drawn, and the record card says so.
- Rotation: NOT normalized. Only a +-10 degree tolerance: the candidate is also tried rotated by -10 and +10 degrees (fixed-point sin and cos), keeping the best. The tolerance covers a hand that holds the Kindle at a different angle on a lap and on a desk, which 2-3 samples drawn in one sitting cannot cover.
  - So V and ^ differ: 156-158 per mille apart in the prototype, against accept thresholds of at most 95.
  - So do < and >, M and W, N and a turned Z, S and a mirrored S.
  - Coordinates are logical (rotated) screen px (map() applies panel_to_logical), so "up" is the user's up, upright or sideways.
- Scale and position: invariant. A shape is the same at 20 mm and 120 mm, anywhere on the page. Its box centre is passed as the anchor (x, y) to editor_shortcut_at, so zoom-in anchors there.

Multi-stroke: NO. A lift ends a shape, as it ends every one-finger thing in Grimoire.
- Waiting after a lift for a possible second stroke would delay or swallow the tap that follows a link, the bar's "tap the page to stay" and panel taps. It would break the plan's rule that nothing ever waits.
- A second stroke's landing cannot be told from a tap.
- The trail needs a definite end to be cleaned.
- Single strokes already give dozens of distinct basic shapes.
In recording, a refused straight stroke followed within 700 ms by another stroke is reported as "One stroke, without lifting." (an X or = drawn in two strokes).

Templates: 2 or 3 samples per gesture, all kept. The gesture distance D_g(c) is the minimum over its samples and the three rotations.

Per-gesture accept threshold:
- spread_g = the largest pairwise distance among its samples.
- T_g = clamp(1.3 x spread_g + 30, 70, 95) per mille.
- Recording-like samples gave spreads of 25-58 in the prototype. A recording whose samples disagree by more than 60 is refused as inconsistent. That bounds T_g at 95: a loose recording can never become a loose gesture.

Decision at runtime, all of these required:
1. The gates (section 3).
2. The best gesture g1 has D1 <= T_g1.
3. Margin: the second-best gesture (another action) has D2 - D1 >= max(35, 0.3 x D1). Otherwise "unclear", and nothing fires.
4. Structure guard: the candidate's path/diagonal ratio lies within 0.6x-1.6x of g1's sample mean. A spiral cannot fire a circle; a double loop cannot fire a single one.
Anything else is a reject: the trail fades and nothing happens. An unknown shape never does anything.

Cost:
- Prototype, host (Apple M5 Pro), with the first pass bounded at T_MAX + 35 so far templates abandon early, and rotations tried only for gestures within 1.5x their threshold:
  - 8 shapes x 3 samples: 0.34-0.44 ms;
  - the 32-shape ceiling: 1.45-1.87 ms.
- With the plan's x20 host-to-Kindle convention, that is about 7-9 ms typical and 29-37 ms worst case on one MT8512 core.
- It runs once per lift, never per frame. The pen is away by definition, and work_pump is called every 4 templates, so it sits far inside the pen's roughly 100 ms evdev budget.

======================================================================
5. NEVER BY ACCIDENT: THE LAYERS, AND THE SLIP BANK
======================================================================
The prototype found the central risk. Shapes with one turn or one arc are exactly what a slip of the finger draws: V, ^, <, >, check mark, L, U, C, 7. A thumb arcs while scrolling; a swipe hooks at its end; a hand skids and turns.

With such shapes recorded (no slip rule), synthetic accidents fired:
- thumb arcs: 110 of 3334 (3.3%);
- one-turn slides: 186 of 3333 (5.6%);
- palm-like drifts: 98 of 3333.
An earlier run with stricter thresholds gave 6.7% and 7.6% for the first two.

The rule: THE SLIP BANK, run at record time. fingershape.c generates a fixed, deterministic bank of slips:
- one-turn slides: turn 30-175 degrees in 10 degree steps, at 20-80% of the path in 15% steps;
- arcs: 40-220 degrees in 20 degree steps;
- every 20 degrees of orientation (the +-10 degree tolerance fills the gaps).
That is about 1500 paths, generated on the fly with no table.

A new recording is refused when any bank path comes within its accept threshold T_g. The reason shown: "Too easy to make by accident." with the hint "Give it two turns or a loop." This replaces vague richness rules: I tried total turning and turn-event counts, and finger wobble made both unreliable. The bank tests the exact property that matters, "could a single slip fire this?", with the real matcher.

Results (10 recordings of each shape):
- Every one-turn shape (V, ^, check, <, >, L, U, C, 7) is refused 10 of 10.
- These are accepted in 9 or 10 of 10 recordings: N, Z, S, circle, zigzag, alpha, square, 2, spiral.
- Triangle, M, W, e and the question mark are sometimes refused.
- Star and pigtail are mostly refused. Their samples vary a lot, so their thresholds are loose, and two legs of a star look like a slip.

With rich shapes recorded through the bank (6 trials of 4-6 shapes, harsh test variation: scale 20-100 mm, +-12 degrees, aspect 0.8-1.25, jitter 0.3-0.8 mm, wobble, start and direction changes, end hooks):
- accepted 92.6%; wrong action 0 of 6200;
- swipes with hooks 0 of 12,000; thumb arcs 0 of 12,000; one-turn slides 2 of 12,000;
- scrubbing 0 of 12,000; palm-like drifts 29 of 12,000;
- deliberate random scribbles 86 of 12,000.
The drifts are why TOUCH_F_BROAD, the palm flag and the pen rules are mandatory, not optional. The P4 freeze requires 0 fires on the owner's writing traces (section 10).

Consequence for the owner: recorded shapes need two turns or a loop. The recognizer itself tells V and ^ apart easily. Allowing one-turn shapes anyway is open question 1.

All layers, strongest first:
1. Context: one fingertip contact, the pen away, starting on the idle page, moving within 400 ms.
2. Gates: size, time, speed, not a line, not tangled.
3. The slip bank at record time.
4. Separation at record time (6.3).
5. Threshold, margin and structure guard at runtime.
6. Shapes act only through editor_shortcut_at's existing gates: idle only, nothing through a keyboard, menus only through their own rules.

======================================================================
6. RECORDING UX: SETTINGS > GESTURES
======================================================================
The sheet is the plan's (step 18: BindKind, the master row, six groups, Reset, Done).

6.1 ROWS
- A row reads "Undo: 2-finger tap" as in the plan. When the action has a finger shape, a 96 x 96 px thumbnail sits in a 120 px column at the row's right.
- A row with only a shape reads "Undo: finger shape" / "Deshacer: figura con el dedo".
- The thumbnail is the medoid sample's 32 points: a 3 px canvas_line_aa polyline, aspect kept, no start dot (direction does not matter).
- A shape line from a newer Grimoire shows "finger shape (newer version)" and no thumbnail.

6.2 THE RECORD CARD
Tap a row: the plan's card, 1400 px wide, upright and sideways.
- Title (64 px): "Do the gesture for Undo" / "Haz el gesto para Deshacer".
- Body (44 px, two lines): "Draw a shape with one finger, swipe or tap with two fingers, or use the pen's button." / "Dibuja una figura con un dedo, desliza o toca con dos dedos, o usa el botón del lápiz."
- Three 260 x 260 sample slots: dashed frames numbered 1 2 3 at 34 px.
- One progress/reason line (44 px, falling back to two lines at 34 px). Only that line is refreshed, by GL16.
- Footer (34 px): "One stroke, without lifting. Two turns or a loop." / "De un trazo, sin levantar el dedo. Dos giros o un bucle."
- Buttons: Use / Try again / Cancel ("Usar" / "Otra vez" / "Cancelar").
- Card height about 1000 px, so it fits sideways (1860).

The shape is drawn anywhere on the screen except the button row, with the same dotted trail as on the page. A touch that starts on a button and moves 6 mm becomes a shape, and the press is dropped.

6.3 THE FLOW
- The first try decides the kind.
  - A two- or three-finger pattern, or a pen gesture, follows the plan exactly: its name at 64 px, then Use / Try again / Cancel.
  - A fast straight one-finger line records as "1 finger right" (TOUCH source).
  - A non-straight one-finger stroke starts a shape.
- Sample 1:
  - The gates run, then a quick slip-bank check at T_MIN (70). That refuses a V at once instead of after three tries.
  - Accepted: slot 1 shows the thumbnail, and the line reads "Good. Draw it again (2 of 3)." / "Bien. Dibújala otra vez (2 de 3)."
- Sample 2 (and 3):
  - It must lie within 60 per mille of an earlier sample. Otherwise: "Not like the first one: draw it again." / "No se parece a la primera: otra vez." The slot stays empty and the earlier samples stay.
  - After sample 2: "Once more makes it surer, or Use." / "Una vez más la afina, o Usar."
- Before Use is enabled, with 2 or 3 samples:
  - (a) Separation against every other action's shape h, with d = the minimum distance from the new samples to h:
    - d <= T_h: "That is the shape for %s. Use moves it here." / "Es la figura de %s. Usar la trae aquí." (the plan's 'Use moves it here' convention). Use then toasts "That shape is no longer for %s." / "Esa figura ya no es para %s."
    - d < max(T_h, T_new) + 20: "Too close to the shape for %s." / "Muy parecida a la figura de %s." The samples are discarded.
  - (b) The full slip-bank check at T_g. It takes about 1-2 s on the Kindle (60-130 ms host x20, about 25% less with 20 degree steps). It is pumped every 64 paths and shows "Checking that a slip cannot draw it..." / "Comprobando que un roce no la trace...". A hit gives "Too easy to make by accident." / "Demasiado fácil de hacer sin querer." plus "Give it two turns or a loop." / "Dale dos giros o un bucle."
- Use:
  - gestures.ini is written atomically, and the map changes only after the write succeeds (the plan's rule). The card closes and the row shows its thumbnail.
  - A new shape replaces the action's old shape. Its touch and pen gestures are untouched, since they are other sources.
- Timeout: 10 s with no attempt at all closes the card and leaves the row as it was. Once one sample exists, there is no timeout.
- Rotating during the card relayouts it and keeps the samples, which are normalized.

6.4 REFUSALS (EN / ES)
Each is short enough for the 1320 px line at 44 px, or two lines at 34 px. CHECK_FIT verifies.
- too small: "Draw it bigger: at least 2 cm across." / "Dibújala más grande: 2 cm o más."
- too slow (over 2.5 s, or under 50 mm/s): "Too slow: draw it in one go." / "Muy lenta: dibújala de una vez."
- late start: "Start moving as soon as you touch." / "Muévete en cuanto toques."
- paused (the cancel): "You held still, so it stopped." / "Te detuviste y se canceló."
- straight, not a valid swipe: "Too straight: give it two turns." / "Muy recta: dale dos giros."
- tangled: "Too many turns: draw a simpler shape." / "Demasiadas vueltas: hazla más simple."
- inconsistent, too close, same as, slip bank: as in 6.3.
- broad contact: "Use a fingertip, not the hand." / "Usa la yema del dedo, no la mano."
- two strokes: "One stroke, without lifting." / "De un trazo, sin levantar el dedo."
- pen near: "The pen is near: move it away." (the plan's).
- late second finger: "Put the fingers down together." (the plan's).
- full: "Grimoire keeps up to 32 shapes." / "Grimoire guarda hasta 32 figuras."

6.5 CLEAR AND RESET
- Holding a row for 0.6 s (ROW_HOLD_MS, library.c:508) clears that row's gestures: touch, shape and pen. A cleared built-in is written as '=nothing'. Toast: "No gestures for %s now." / "Ya no hay gestos para %s." Same shape as forget_row (library.c:726-743).
- Reset gestures deletes gestures.ini. When shapes exist it asks first: "Reset gestures? Your %d finger shapes will be deleted." / "¿Restablecer los gestos? Se borrarán tus %d figuras." (plural forms), with Reset and Cancel. Recorded shapes are the user's own work.

======================================================================
7. FEEDBACK ON THE PAGE
======================================================================
7.1 THE TRAIL
- From PENDING -> DRAWING, round 7 px black dots every 20 px with a 2 px white halo, drawn with step 6's canvas_dash_poly in a dot mode.
- They go into App.screen only: never into page_canvas, never a stroke. Any compose() erases them. The trail can never become ink, and never reaches the .qpg, the PDF, thumbnails or the sleep image.
- Flushes: the dots added since the last flush, as app_invalidate(rect, REFRESH_FAST) and then an app_flush of their own at once, as app_keyboard_pointer does for its field. app_invalidate keeps one union at the strongest mode (app.c:911-917), so a trail frame must never merge into someone's GL16.
- At most one trail flush every 40 ms (25 Hz).
- These are plain DU frames: not live ink, no pen mode. display_fbink.c dithers the changed pixels and leaves unchanged ones undriven (display_fbink.c:503-509).
- The first frame draws the path since landing, so the trail appears whole, about 0.35 s after landing at the earliest.

7.2 A MATCH
- compose(a, trail_rect), then app_invalidate(trail_rect, REFRESH_UI), then the action through editor_shortcut_at(a, action, cx, cy, SRC_SHAPE). The cleanup GL16 and the action's own refresh go out together. When the action redraws the whole screen (page turn, Pages view), the trail rides its refresh.
- Then a small toast names the action: its registry label ("Undo" / "Deshacer") for 1200 ms. It is skipped when:
  - the action toasted itself (a->toast_until changed during the dispatch);
  - or it opened a full-screen view (Pages view, Index map, Library).
- SRC_SHAPE never creates a page from next-page (the plan's SRC_TOUCH and SRC_PEN rule). At the end of the notebook: "This is the last page."
- When editor_shortcut_at refuses the action (it returns false: a sheet, a keyboard, the wrong menu), it is treated as a reject.

7.3 A REJECT (the fade on e-ink)
- At the lift, compose the trail rect and redraw every other dot: one DU frame. Only the removed dots' pixels change, so only they are driven, and the trail visibly thins.
- 250 ms later (editor_tick), GL16 of the trail rect. GL16 drives the remaining black dots through the gray levels to the page: they fade out over its 271 ms, with no flash.
- Total about 0.7 s, clearly different from a match, which cleans at once and shows a toast.
- No toast, except once ever (hints bit 7): "That is not one of your finger shapes. Settings > Gestures lists them." / "No es una de tus figuras. Ajustes > Gestos las muestra."

7.4 ABORTS
- Second finger or pinch: the trail rect joins the pinch's first refresh, or a GL16 when the pinch never commits.
- Pen arrival: restore by DU, and add the rect to S->settle. A GL16 must not race the pen's next stroke onto the slow path (the plan's rule: never GL16 while the pen is down). The writing settle GL16s it.
- Sleep, rotation, leaving the editor: no refresh. The screen is redrawn anyway; editor_suspend, editor_enter and editor_leave reset the capture.

7.5 MENUS
- Shapes act through open menus exactly as a key bound to the same action does (editor_shortcut, editor.c:1974-2010).
- Of the menus, only the Links bar leaves the page live under a finger. There:
  - a finger that moves past 6 mm becomes a shape, not a "tap the page to stay" (the hotbar plan commits only within the 30 px slop);
  - its lift dispatches as a key would: the bar's own shape closes it back to the origin page (D2's cancel), another menu's shape swaps, anything else is refused and fades.
- Every other sheet keeps its own finger rules, and shapes never start there.
- The Pages view, the Index map, the Library and Settings: no shapes in v1, except the record card.

7.6 FLASH BUDGET
One GL16 per shape. It counts toward the every-30th promotion (app.c:931), like every UI GL16. DU frames do not. GC16 never.

======================================================================
8. STORAGE: gestures.ini
======================================================================
The plan's file and grammar (shortcuts.ini's: '#' and ';' comments, trimmed key=value, a later duplicate wins, keys case-insensitive), in root/ beside shortcuts.ini and controller.ini, absorbing pen.ini (D8).

Shape lines are keyed by ACTION, not by gesture. A recorded shape has no name; its data is its identity. One shape per action matches the binding rule.

  # Grimoire: gestures (Settings > Gestures). Built in unless a line says otherwise:
  # touch.2.down=pages, touch.2.up=links, touch.2.left=next-page, touch.2.right=previous-page, pen.Button.triple=clear-page, pen.Button.hold=clear-page
  # shape.ACTION=1,N,S1,S2[,S3]: a finger shape you drew; format 1, N samples; each sample is 32 points in drawing order, x then y as two hex digits, the larger side spanning 00-ff.
  touch.2.tap=undo
  pen.Button.double=links
  shape.undo=1,3,1607180331034c00660581079b0ab609d00cea04ec17d829cb3fba53a66592777c86689855ab44bf34d41ee312f62cf447f362f57cf995ffb0fdc7fae0fbedf7,<128 hex>,<128 hex>
(That sample is a real Z from the prototype: 46 raw frames resampled to 32.)

Format 1:
- the version;
- N, 2 or 3;
- exactly N samples of 128 hex digits (case-insensitive).
Points are stored bbox-normalized to 0-255, centred, aspect kept. The 8-bit step is 0.4% of the size, negligible against thresholds of 7-9.5%. Drawing order is stored although matching ignores it: thumbnails are polylines, and a later direction-aware format needs no re-recording.

Derived at load (fs_prepare), never stored:
- the clouds, spread_g, T_g, the path/diagonal ratio;
- computed by integer math, so every device derives the same thresholds;
- about 3 ms per shape on the Kindle; lazy on first use when there are many.

Validation:
- Refused and counted (toasted when the sheet opens, as the plan does), and gone at the next write: a version 1 line with
  - the wrong count, bad hex, or a degenerate sample (a box under 32 units on both axes);
  - an action the registry has without SHAPE.
- Carried verbatim and written back:
  - a well-formed line with an unknown version, or an action this version does not know (from a newer Grimoire);
  - each up to 1 KiB, 16 KiB in all (the plan's 2 KiB carry is too small for shape lines of about 420 B).
- Recording a shape for an action that holds a carried newer line replaces it, and the card warns: "This replaces a shape from a newer Grimoire."

Limits:
- 64 KiB file (the plan's bounded reader);
- 32 shape lines (FS_SHAPES_MAX), about 13.5 KB at most;
- an unreadable file runs without shapes and the built-in gestures, is never overwritten, and the sheet offers Reset (the plan's rule).
Read in app_init, on the Controller sheet's Reload, and whenever the Gestures sheet opens.

Beside the built-ins and the pen (D6, D8):
- touch.* and pen.* stay gesture -> action overlays over built-ins that are never written.
- shape.* has no built-ins. A built-in shape would fire by accident for people who never asked, and would take shape space from them.
- The runtime classes never compete:
  - two- and three-finger patterns come from touchgest as IN_GESTURE;
  - a one-finger stroke is either a straight swipe (touch.1.*) or a shape;
  - pen gestures come from the pen lane.
- Binding rule (the plan's, with one more source): per source, a binding does one action, and an action has at most one binding per source. So Pages can be "2 fingers down" (built in) and a finger shape and a pen double-click at once. That is exactly what D5 needs where the page scrolls.

======================================================================
9. THE SIDEWAYS WHOLE-PAGE SETTING (D5)
======================================================================
What it does: when the Kindle is sideways, the resting view shows the whole page instead of filling the width. Nothing scrolls, so the plan's touchgest view context has scrolls_v and scrolls_h false, and two-finger swipes (Pages, Links, page turns) work anywhere on the screen, sideways as upright. On by default; the owner must be told (P2 test notes, plus a one-time hint).

Code:
- view_reset (editor.c:523-531):
    zoom_default = (st->landscape_fit && a->w > a->h) ? zoom_min : a->w / pgw;
- A new S->zoom_max = 4 x (a->w / pgw) keeps today's ceiling. view_clamp (editor.c:504-518) and pinch (editor.c:2321) clamp to zoom_max instead of zoom_default x 4.
- zoomed() (editor.c:546) still compares against zoom_default. So Fit page returns to the whole page, and the editor.zoom probe (editor.c:2635) reads 1.00 there.
- The page sits centred (1395 px wide at 0.75 on a 2480 px screen). The floating panel sits over the desk on the right and no longer covers ink.

settings.ini: landscape_fit 0|1, default 1.
- Appended after the plan's new keys, undotted, missing means 1.
- 1.0.0-beta drops it, so the default comes back (the plan's convention).
- store.c: read beside pinch_zoom (1896), written after it (2031), default in settings_defaults (1692).
- Probe: settings.landscape_fit (app.c:1022-1037).

Where it lives: the Display sheet, a checkbox row after "Invert colors": "Sideways, show the whole page" / "De lado, ver la página entera".
- Settings has no room: library.c:997 says the language row is the last that fits sideways.
- The Display sheet has room: row_h (dispmenu.c:34-40) still gets its 140 px maximum with 8 rows, sideways (1398 / 8 = 174) and upright.
- It is reachable from the editor's panel, so the owner can flip it while sideways and see the effect.

Action: landscape-fit. TOGGLE, Pages group (7 -> 8 rows, under the 11-row limit), sources KEY | PAD | TOUCH | SHAPE | PEN.
- Label: "Whole page sideways" / "Página entera de lado".
- Toasts:
  - on: "Sideways shows the whole page." / "De lado se ve la página entera.";
  - off: "Sideways fills the width." / "De lado ocupa todo el ancho.";
  - toggled upright: "Applies when the Kindle is sideways." / "Se aplica con el Kindle de lado."
- In P2 it joins step 7's new names, so keys can bind it at once. Gestures and shapes can from P4.

On rotate: editor_enter calls view_reset when the screen size changes (editor.c:2243). Turning sideways lands on the whole page with the rotation's usual GC16; turning upright is unchanged.

Toggling while sideways: view_reset plus compose_all(REFRESH_FULL), as Fit page does (editor.c:2045-2048), even if the user had pinched in. They pressed it to see the result.

Pinch while on: pinch zoom works as today when pinch_zoom is on, from the whole page up to zoom_max; zooming out stops at the whole page.
- Zoomed in, the view scrolls. Mid-screen two-finger drags pan, the navigation swipes start in the plan's edge bands, and finger shapes plus the panel's Pages and Links buttons still open those anywhere.
- A page turn (view_reset at editor.c:830), Fit page or a rotation returns to the whole page. The setting itself never changes by pinching.

One-time hint, the first time the Kindle turns sideways after the update (hints bit 8): "Sideways now shows the whole page, so two-finger swipes work. Pinch to zoom in; Display changes this." / "De lado ahora se ve la página entera y los gestos de dos dedos funcionan. Pellizca para ampliar; se cambia en Pantalla."

Scenarios: 25 scenarios rotate. Those whose expectations depend on the width fit sideways get the header line '# settings: landscape_fit=0': at least f_batch2, y_all_screens, y_pagesize_1_ksc, y_pagesize_2_back and z_4_erase_zoom_rotate, which rotate and check zoom or pinch. The rest are audited by running the suite.

======================================================================
10. TESTABILITY
======================================================================
10.1 UNIT: tests/test_fingershape.c, pure, host.
- Gates on both sides of every edge:
  - box 19/21 mm, path 29/31 mm;
  - lead 390/410 ms, duration 2490/2510 ms, pause 490/510 ms;
  - speed 45/55 mm/s;
  - chord deviation 14/16%, tangle 4.9/5.1x;
  - trail delay 140/160 ms, shape slop 5.5/6.5 mm.
- Invariances:
  - translation; scale x5;
  - rotation +-9 degrees accepted, +-25 degrees rejected (on Z);
  - circle CW = CCW;
  - a closed shape started at 4 points = one gesture;
  - V vs ^ D >= 2 x T_MAX.
- The codec: round trip, case, a bad count, bad hex, a degenerate sample, an unknown version carried, the carry limits.
- Record checks: consistency (55/65), the separation tiers, the slip bank refusing V, ^, check, <, >, L, U and C and passing N, Z, S and circle.
- Determinism: fixed inputs give exact D values (integer math). The same asserted numbers pass on the Mac and on the Linux CI.
- A shared-constants assertion: record and runtime use one table.
- A bench: host microseconds for 8 and for 32 shapes, with a ceiling assertion (2.5 ms host for 32 x 3).

10.2 SYNTHETIC CORPUS: src/fingershape_synth.c, shared by the unit test and the runner.
- 26 single-stroke shapes, as in the prototype.
- A finger model: 75-80 Hz frames, a minimum-jerk speed profile, jitter, low-frequency wobble, corner rounding, end hooks, start shift and reversal for closed shapes.
- Two variation regimes: "recording" and "use".
- Slip kinds: swipe with a hook, thumb arc, one-turn slide or hairpin, palm-like drift, scrub; plus random scribbles as the hard case.
- Fixed seeds. The jitter, rate and speed parameters are re-fitted from the P1 traces before the freeze.
- Gates asserted, at least the prototype's results:
  - accept >= 92% under "use" variation, >= 97% under "recording" variation;
  - wrong action 0;
  - swipes, thumb arcs, slides and scrubs: 0 per 12,000 each. The prototype's 2 slide fires must be removed by the freeze tuning;
  - palm-like drifts at most 1 per 1000 for the shape layer alone. The prototype gives 2.4 per 1000; the device gates and traces close the rest.

10.3 DEVICE TRACES. P1 step 1 gains an opt-in, owner-created empty file grimoire/touch-trace (like the smart-shapes plan's shape-log).
- While input is grabbed (never at the PIN, input_evdev.c:136-137), Grimoire appends grimoire/touch-trace.txt:
    # grimoire touch-trace 1, rotation R, WxH, dpi D
    F <k_ms> <slot>:<id>:<x>:<y>:<major>:<tool> ...   (logical px, one line per SYN_REPORT with contacts)
    P <k_ms> prox|down|up|leave                        (pen state only; never pen coordinates, so no handwriting)
    E <k_ms> <outcome>                                 (fshape outcomes, for auditing)
- Capped at 4 MB, never exported, deleted by deleting the file.
- The owner script in docs/KINDLE.md adds:
  - each of Z, N, S, circle, alpha and triangle with one finger, 10 times;
  - 10 one-finger swipes each way;
  - 10 one-finger V shapes (for open question 1);
  - 5 minutes of writing with the palm resting, lifting the pen between lines;
  - 2 minutes holding the Kindle while reading and turning pages.
- Runner: 'trace FILE' replays F lines through touchgest as contact frames, on the virtual clock from the k_ms deltas, and P lines into the pen context.
- Fixtures go to tests/fixtures/touch/ after review. They hold touch coordinates only.
- Criteria:
  - with a stress set of 8 recorded shapes, the writing, holding and reading traces fire 0 times;
  - the owner's shape traces, with 3 samples recorded and the rest tested, accept >= 95% with 0 wrong.
- The 74 one-finger drags in the 16 existing logs (read-time stamps, first 120 touch events per session) become tests/fixtures/touch/legacy-drags.qs, generated by a script from ~/KindleLab/evidence: 0 fires against the stress set.

10.4 RUNNER AND SIMULATOR
- Commands:
  - 'shape NAME X Y SIZE_MM [MS] [ROT] [SEED] [REV]': a synthetic shape as one-contact frames through touchgest;
  - 'fpath X1 Y1 X2 Y2 ... [MS]': an exact polyline, for edge tests;
  - 'trace FILE'.
  The plan's 'finger', 'swipe', 'tapn', 'pen hover' and 'pen leave' combine with them (a pen hover during a shape, a second finger mid-shape).
- Probes:
  - fshape.last: '<fired|reject|refused|cancel> <action|reason> <d1> <thr> <d2>';
  - fshape.fired: the count since the last check;
  - fshape.state; fshape.trail ('x y w h' or empty);
  - gestures.shape.ACTION (the sample count, empty for none);
  - gestures.shape_count;
  - settings.landscape_fit.
  - display.presents (keyboard lane) proves the refresh plan: fast frames, then ui, never full.
- The simulator window: the right button is already the finger (sim_sdl.c), so shapes are drawn with a right-drag. SDL trackpad fingers stay optional.

10.5 SCENARIOS
- s_shape_1_record: record Z for Undo three times. The slots fill, Use writes shape.undo, the row thumbnail is shot.
- s_shape_2_fire: draw ink, then 'pen leave', wait 1100, shape Z. The stroke count drops by one, the toast says Undo, display.presents is fast..., ui with no full.
- s_shape_3_reject: shape S unrecorded. Nothing changes; fshape.last is reject; a DU, then a GL16 250 ms later.
- s_shape_4_guards, each giving nothing:
  - pen hovering;
  - starting on the panel;
  - a second finger at 200 ms (trail cleaned);
  - a 450 ms rest before moving;
  - 3 s total (the trail thins while down);
  - a 600 ms pause.
  Also: a tap on a link still follows it, and a 600 ms hold still opens the card.
- s_shape_5_refusals:
  - V gives 'Too easy to make by accident';
  - small gives 'Draw it bigger';
  - inconsistent gives 'Not like the first one';
  - Z for Redo while Undo has Z gives 'Use moves it here' and a toast;
  - a near shape gives 'Too close'.
- s_shape_6_scroll: sideways, pinched in. A mid-screen two-finger drag pans; the shape bound to pages opens Pages.
- s_shape_7_bar: with the Links bar open, the bar's own shape closes it to the origin; another shape fades; tap-to-stay still commits.
- s_shape_8_es: the card, rows and refusals in Spanish, upright and sideways, both styles, under CHECK_FIT.
- s_shape_9_traces: the fixtures and legacy drags fire 0 times.
- s_fit_1:
  - rotate 1: editor.zoom is 1.00 at zoom_min, and swipe 2 down mid-screen opens Pages;
  - pinch in, then a page turn returns to the whole page;
  - Display toggle off gives the width fit; the landscape-fit key toggles it;
  - the hint appears once.

======================================================================
11. RISKS
======================================================================
- One-turn shapes are refused by default. The owner may want a V. The recognizer keeps V and ^ apart easily; the refusal is about accidents. Open question 1.
- An unrecorded but similar deliberate shape fires the similar recorded one: 7.6% in the prototype; a square fires a recorded circle (53 per mille apart). Separation stops both being recorded, but drawing a square when only a circle exists may fire the circle's action. The record card says shapes are matched by how they look.
- Synthetic palm-like drifts reach the matcher at 2.4 per 1000. Safety rests on TOUCH_F_BROAD (T_palm unknown until the P1 log), the palm flag and the pen rules. Shapes do not ship until the writing traces fire 0 times.
- The bank check takes about 1-2 s on the Kindle at Use. It is pumped and shows progress; it could move to a bgjob if the device timing is worse.
- Thresholds were tuned on synthetic fingers. 75 Hz centroids near the bezel compress. The freeze waits for the traces.
- landscape_fit changes today's sideways default. Mitigated by the hint, the Display row, the action, and the P2 test notes. Five or more rotate scenarios need the header line.
- Live view streams App.screen, so viewers see the trail (the plan already notes this for the bar).

steps.title: [P4, new step 18a] fingershape.c: the pure capture, gates, matcher and record checks
steps.detail:
New src/fingershape.c/.h in CORE_SRC, plus src/fingershape_synth.c (sim, runner and tests only). Integer math only.

- fs_prepare: spread, T_g = clamp(1.3 x spread + 30, 70, 95), ratio.
- fs_match: threshold, margin max(35, 0.3 D1), structure guard 0.6-1.6x.
- fs_record_check: consistency 60, separation (same-as at T_h; too-close under max(T_h, T_new) + 20), and the deterministic slip bank (one-turn slides and arcs every 20 degrees, generated on the fly, pumped every 64).

open_questions: Shapes with one turn or one arc (V, ^, <, >, check mark, L, U, C) are refused by default, with 'Too easy to make by accident'. In the prototype every one of them was within reach of a single finger slip, and with them recorded, 3-6% of synthetic thumb arcs and one-turn slides fired an action. Keep them refused (recommended until the device traces measure real slips), or add a 'Use anyway' button that saves one with stricter gates (25 mm minimum, 250 ms lead, pen away 3 s)?
